plain_english_policy: This bill authorizes local school boards in Alabama to designate specific employees as 'school security personnel' who are permitted to carry firearms while on duty at K-12 schools and on related buses. To qualify, these individuals must complete 16 hours of approved firearm training and pass annual requalification tests similar to law enforcement officers. The State Department of Education is mandated to cover all costs associated with this training, including paid time off for employees.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would expand the legal authority within Alabama public schools beyond licensed concealed carry permit holders or sworn law enforcement officers by creating a new category of authorized armed staff (school security personnel). This shifts some responsibility for school safety from solely relying on external police presence to allowing trained internal employees to be armed, funded directly by state resources.
sponsorship_supports_position: The sponsors affirmatively advanced legislation expanding the ability of designated school staff to carry firearms under specific training requirements.
evidence_quotes: "This bill would authorize a local board of education to designate employees as school security personnel and would allow such persons designated as school security personnel...to carry firearms while on duty."

"A local board of education may allow any person employed by the board as school security personnel to carry a firearm while on duty if the employee satisfies all of the following qualifications: (1) He or she has attended, and successfully completed, 16 hours of firearm training..."
